name: Safed Maas
instructions: 1. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and add whole spices (cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon) until fragrant.
2. Add the mutton pieces and sear until they change color, then add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a few minutes.
3. Lower the heat and slowly incorporate the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
4. Add the cashew and melon seed pastes and cook on low heat until the meat is tender and the oil starts to separate.
5. Season with white pepper, mace powder, and salt.
6. Finally, stir in the fresh cream to achieve a creamy white texture and simmer for 5 minutes.
7. Garnish with a few dried rose petals and serve hot with sheermal or khamiri roti.
description: Safed Maas is a signature dish of the royal kitchens of Rajasthan. Unlike the fiery red Lal Maas, this dish is defined by its elegant, creamy white color and a subtle, sophisticated flavor profile achieved by using white pepper and nut pastes instead of red chilies.
